headline_marked: OpenAI launches [[next-gen voice models]] for more natural ChatGPT conversations
headline: OpenAI launches next-gen voice models for more natural ChatGPT conversations
summary: New GPT-Live-1 models enable simultaneous speaking and listening for seamless interruptions and live translation, replacing ChatGPT's default Advanced Voice Mode.
details: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, new conversational voice models designed to sound more natural and improve turn-taking in ChatGPT. These full-duplex models can speak and listen concurrently, allowing for natural interruptions and facilitating features like real-time translation.

The GPT-Live-1 mini will become the default for ChatGPT's Advanced Voice Mode, while paid users will gain access to the more advanced GPT-Live-1 model. This upgrade moves beyond the previous system of separate speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech models.

OpenAI states the new models address previous limitations, such as interrupting users mid-sentence or lacking conversational intelligence. The system can now query newer GPT models like GPT-5.5 for search and reasoning while maintaining conversation flow.

The models are designed for extended interactions, with OpenAI's voice product lead reporting conversations lasting 30-40 minutes. OpenAI envisions voice as a primary interface for complex computing tasks and agentic work, potentially paving the way for future AI hardware.

While competitors like Apple and Amazon are also enhancing their voice assistants, OpenAI's focus is on making ChatGPT's voice mode more conversational and hands-free. Safeguards are built-in for age-appropriateness and to handle sensitive topics.

Despite advancements, some limitations were noted, such as an unnatural accent during a Hindi live translation demo. OpenAI is optimizing for 'most spoken languages' but has not specified which ones will receive full support.
